name: Lengilu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Mortensen, Christian John. 2021. The Kemaloh Lun Bawang language of Borneo. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (chair R. Blust). 315 pp. hdl:10125/75955
sources.note: §3.4 (pp. 51-54) is about Kemaloh Lun Bawang, not Lengilu': 'Kemaloh Lun Bawang stress is not contrastive and appears, from the available data, to usually fall on a word's final syllable' with a few penult exceptions (pelanuk, buayeh, lematek). §3.4.1 p. 52: 'in many of the modern Dayic dialects, stress appears to be predominantly final, especially in... the Sa'ban varieties... and the dialects of the upper Padi River'. p. 224: Ulu Padi erosion presupposes 'a stress shift away from a Lun Bawang-like pattern... to a much more lopsided pattern, with heavy stress on the ultima'. §11.4.3 Lengilu'…

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. Peta Bahasa: Provinsi Kalimantan Utara (11 languages).
sources.note: Lengilu is not listed among the 11 languages of Kalimantan Utara (Abai, Bugis, Bulungan, Kenyah, Long Pulung, Lundayeh,...), so no Indonesian national-agency description exists under this name.

sources.citation: Marzuki, Ernisa. 2024 (21 Oct). Sounds from a lost tribe: documenting the Lengilo. UNIMAS Gazette, Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (on the study by Nur Ardini Jian, Hamidah Abdul Wahab & Ting Su Hie).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reports a preliminary phonological inventory of 'Lengilo' spoken among Lun Bawang in Sarawak (one 80-year-old informant): 'six types of consonants, three types of vowels, and three types of diphthongs', no affricates; <150 speakers claimed.

sources.citation: Mortensen, Christian. 2019. sources.note: Raw field notebook, no prose statement. Notebook pp. 1-4 headed 'Lengilu' (Long Layu' LL, Long Padi LP)' give Lun Dayeh headwords with Lengilu' IPA transcriptions that carry a stress mark on the final syllable throughout, as far as I could read the handwriting: [la'wɑɪ] 'lawé', [i'kɔh] 'iko', [da'ʔət] 'dat', [ta'ʔʊrn] 'tawan', [kəmə'kar] 'kemekar', [bə'rək] 'berek', [na'lan] 'nalan', [la'wɪd] 'lawid', [tə'fuh] 'tebpuh', [pə'hũŋ] 'pegung', [la'ʔʊd] 'lod', [ki'təh], [me'duh], [mə'laɪt], [mə'sɪŋ], [ma'daw]. Marginal note next to uih [ak']: 'Final stress? Sa: [ɛ̃k]'. First-hand data consistent wi…

sources.note: Nothing on stress; states 'Lengilu, reportedly an aberrant North Sarawak language similar to Sa'ban, although no published data of any kind are available to test this claim' (4 speakers, 2000).

sources.citation: Clayre, Beatrice. 2005. Kelabitic languages and the fate of 'focus': evidence from the Kerayan. In I Wayan Arka & Malcolm Ross (eds), The many faces of Austronesian voice systems: some new empirical studies, 17-57. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics (PL 571).
sources.note: Nothing. Spells the name 'Lengilo'' (dialects B. Liku, Binuang, Lg Padi, Lg Mutan; 1995 survey). Fn 46, p. 37: 'The Kerayan dialects have not yet been analysed phonemically, and spelling in this paper generally follows the system devised by Blust for Kelabit.' §4 lists segmental changes (initial-syllable loss etc.), no prosody.

sources.note: The only phonological description of a variety called Lengilo (consonant/vowel/diphthong inventories from one 80-year-old speaker); a 'deskripsi awal' in Malay would normally include a tekanan (stress) note. Identity caveat: speakers live among Lun Bawang at Lawas/Ba'Kelalan, Sarawak, and the companion study finds 94.6% lexical identity with Lun Bawang, so this may not be the Krayan Lengilu' of leng1260.
